use: Month by month, the middle resale house price stayed between about $333,000 and $368,000, and the condo price between about $197,000 and $225,000.

use: The federal house price index for Horry County rose about 51 percent from mid-2021 to mid-2025. In the year to mid-2026 it was about flat, up 0.8 percent, which is less than the index's own margin.

struck: House prices in the Myrtle Beach metro rose 0.8 percent in the year to mid-2026.
use: In the year to mid-2026 the index was about flat, up 0.8 percent, which is less than the index's own margin.

struck: For homes already listed, the miss falls to 1.65 percent, because the estimate can see the list price.
use: For homes already listed, the middle miss was 1.65 percent. Redfin says its estimate is more accurate for homes for sale because more data is available about them.

struck: Online estimates miss here too.
use: (say whose figures they are: Redfin's own published accuracy for its own estimate; do not apply them to online estimates in general)

struck: On a $350,000 house, 10 percent is $35,000.
use: On a $350,000 house, the county value's middle miss for houses, 9 percent, is about $31,000.

struck: The county does it every four years and puts the new values into effect in the fifth.
use: State law has each county revalue every property once every five years.

pattern: limit does not apply that year
struck: The county values a sold home as of December 31 of the year it sold, and the 15 percent limit does not apply that year.
use: The county values a sold home as of December 31 of the year it sold. That value is first taxed the next year, and the 15 percent limit does not hold it down.

pattern: 15 percent in five years, even when
struck: Between sales, a reassessment can raise the taxable value of a home by no more than 15 percent in five years, even when the market rose more.
use: Between sales, a reassessment can raise the taxable value of a home by no more than 15 percent in five years. The value of an addition or improvement is added on top.

struck: Homes last sold before 2005 are taxed on about 59 percent of it.
use: Homes whose last deed on the county record is from before 2005 are taxed on about 59 percent of it.

struck: So a seller's tax bill says little about what the home is worth, or what the buyer will pay.
use: So the taxable value on a seller's bill is often far below the county's own market value.

struck: A buyer prices in their own bill, not the seller's.
use: (cut it: a claim about buyers' behavior with no source)

struck: A home you live in is taxed on 4 percent of its value.
use: A home its owner lives in is assessed at 4 percent of its value, once the owner applies and qualifies.

struck: Condos within about a block of the water (under 0.1 mile) ask a middle $322 a square foot; the first-row condos are smaller.
use: Condos within 0.1 mile of the ocean ask a middle $322 a square foot, and they are smaller.

struck: Asking price per square foot doubles from two miles inland to the first row.
use: Asking price per square foot is about twice as high for condos within 0.1 mile of the ocean as for condos more than 2 miles away, and about 2.5 times as high for houses.

use: About 13 percent of homes resold in the county sat inside FEMA's high-risk flood zone: 1 in 4 condos and 1 in 15 houses.

pattern: tell you in writing|cannot be used to get a mortgage
struck: An agent may give you a value for your home, but must tell you in writing that it cannot be used to get a mortgage.
use: An agent may give you a value for your home if it is not called an appraisal, and must give you this sentence: "This valuation service may not be used for the purposes of obtaining financing in a federally related transaction."

struck: In South Carolina only a licensed appraiser may do one or call themselves an appraiser.
use: In South Carolina, appraisal work and the title of appraiser need an appraiser's license. An agent may give a valuation only if it is not called an appraisal.

struck: The buyer has the right to a free copy, no later than three days before closing.
use: The buyer gets a free copy as soon as it is done, or three business days before closing if that is sooner, unless the buyer agrees in advance to get it at closing.

struck: What a first-row condo sells: the view from a high floor straight onto the beach.
use: The beach in Myrtle Beach from a high floor of an oceanfront building.
